answer: Cap each epoch's admissions at a fixed count of seats auctioned by sealed bid. Because the pearl supply never grows, a bidder's own volume sets the uniform price all pay. An operator spreading clones across many seats lodges many umber sealed bids at once; that bulk demand drags the clearing price to a higher opal paid on every seat held, so cost per identity rises with its own order size. The protocol never learns which seats one hand controls, yet that pressure is self-inflicted; a lone bidder barely moves it. At settlement each bid is repriced and burned, so no seat pools across coalitions.
